summary: Master NGO staff well-being and duty of care. Learn to manage vicarious trauma and psychosocial risks using ISO 45003 and ProQOL. Enroll today.
lede: NGO staff well-being and mental health training helps HR, operations, safeguarding and program leaders assess psychosocial risks and plan practical support for staff. Participants learn to map workplace stressors, distinguish vicarious trauma from compassion fatigue, and develop peer support, crisis response and trauma-informed supervision approaches. The course also covers resilience practices and integrating well-being measures into daily operations and organizational planning.
audienceIntro: This program is essential for professionals responsible for the health, safety, and operational effectiveness of personnel in the non-profit and humanitarian sectors.
audience: Employee Well-being Specialists focused on the non-profit
modules: Foundations of NGO Duty of Care
Managing Vicarious Trauma and Compassion Fatigue
Psychological First Aid in the Workplace
Well-being in Remote and Field Operations
Digital Tools and AI for Staff Support
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 3 years of experience in a management, HR, or operational role within the NGO or humanitarian sector. Familiarity with basic organizational policies and personnel management is required. No prior clinical mental health training is necessary.
